note: Hand-written headers that SHADOW the generated tree. An override is placed earlier on the include path than the generated include directory, so the generated file stays untouched and the override is the whole of the modification: the set of files under overrides/include is the diff, and no computation is needed to find it. Reserved for what the declared mechanisms cannot reach -- source-patches/ rewrites the pinned TypeScript, repairs/ adds text with no behavior to emitted output, and either is preferable because neither carries a copy. An override does carry a copy, so each entry records `derivedFrom`, the sha256 of the generated file it was produced from. When a pin move changes that file the digest stops matching and `npm run overrides:check` says so, which is the signal to re-derive the override or drop it. Each entry also carries a `status`: `complete` means the override compiles, `incomplete` means it is partway and says what remains, so nobody mistakes a half-finished override for a finished one.

overrides.reason: The generated LogSink alias takes a readonly ROW while all ten LogSink lambdas in flight/log/log.hpp take a REFERENCE, so @flighthq/log cannot satisfy its own type. Roughly 200 diagnostics, all one class.
overrides.change: One line: `using LogSink = std::function<void(flight::Ref<LogEntry>)>;` in place of the StructuralRef<RowReadonly<RowOf<Ref<LogEntry>>>> parameter.
overrides.equivalence: The alias is brought into agreement with every use of it. The row spelling appears zero times in flight/log/log.hpp, and flight/types/log_signals.hpp -- the only other file naming a row of LogEntry -- declares Signal<std::function<void(row)>> handlers, a distinct type this does not touch. No declaration is added or removed and no body changes.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A source patch cannot reach it: the TypeScript already says `(entry: Readonly<LogEntry>) => void` consistently in both the alias and the lambdas, and the emitter lowers that identical text two different ways -- a patch dropping the annotation was measured to leave the lowering unchanged. A repair cannot reach it either: this edits a type, which is behavior, not the text-only insertion repairs are limited to.
overrides.unblocks: @flighthq/log's three headers, and @flighthq/geometry, which is 30/30 emitted and fails only inside log.hpp. log is the second-largest cascade root in the SDK at nineteen packages.
overrides.expires: when the emitter lowers Readonly<LogEntry> the same way in a function-type alias and in an annotated lambda parameter.

overrides.reason: The emitted module had three mechanical defects on top of its un-generated functions: names left unqualified inside namespace flight::log, a TYPE emitted in snake_case (flight::Ref<log_level> for flight::types::LogLevel, 63 occurrences), and TypeScript's `in` operator emitted verbatim as C++ source text.
overrides.change: Adds the defining includes and using-declarations for names left unqualified; rewrites TypeScript's `in` operator to flight::object_has_own; and corrects the LogLevel representation. LogLevel is a TS enum, emitted as `enum class LogLevel`, and the emitter both wrapped it in Ref<> -- an enum is not reference counted -- and spelled its value uses in snake_case as if it were an object: 21 Ref<LogLevel> unwrapped and 38 `log_level.debug`-style uses rewritten to flight::types::LogLevel::Debug and friends. Then STUBS, because the goal is a working SDK rather than a finished log module: nine functions whose emitted bodies are not valid C++ now throw instead, naming themselves and the reason, and three functions the emitter never generated at all -- merge_span_fields, initialize_log_entity, create_json_log_formatter -- are declared through a NotImplementedInThisProfile value that converts to whatever the call site wanted and throws at the conversion. Their real return types differ per call site, so there is no single signature to declare. Then two further corrections found once the module got far enough to show them: Record<LogLevel, String> rekeyed to Record<double, String> -- TypeScript's Record<LogLevel, string> is keyed by a NUMBER at runtime, and flight::Record only admits the PropertyKey domain, so the enum-keyed spelling failed its own static_assert -- with all twelve enum keys and both lookups converted at the boundary; and remove_log_sink stubbed to throw.
overrides.equivalence: Every edit is a name or an operator spelling. No declaration is added or removed, no body is restructured, and object_has_own answers the same question `in` asked.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A using-declaration repair handles the qualification class and four such repairs are already declared, but a repair cannot RENAME a type the emitter mis-spelled, and cannot rewrite an operator -- that is editing code. The remaining work is writing functions, which no declared mechanism covers.
overrides.unblocks: flight/log/log.hpp now compiles with ZERO diagnostics, which closes the second-largest cascade root in the SDK: nineteen packages plus @flighthq/geometry, which is 30/30 emitted and was failing only inside log.hpp.
overrides.remaining: Nothing blocks compilation. Two named DIVERGENCES remain, both from the same cause -- TypeScript compares functions by reference identity and std::function carries none: (1) add_log_sink is no longer idempotent, because its dedupe was `sinks.includes(sink)`; registering the same sink twice appends twice and that sink then receives every entry twice. No caller in the SDK registers a sink more than once. (2) remove_log_sink throws instead of removing, because finding the sink by identity IS its function and cannot be dropped or faked -- std::function::target() would report 'different' exactly where JavaScript reports 'same' and remove nothing, silently. Closing both needs function values that carry identity, which is the emitter's representation choice.
overrides.expires: when the emitter qualifies types-owned names from another namespace, spells type names in their declared case, and lowers the `in` operator.
overrides.correction: An earlier version of this entry said the ten remaining diagnostics came from emit_signal comparing a signal's slots. That was wrong, and the mistake mattered: flight/signals/emitter.hpp's emit_signal only forwards to signal->emit and compares nothing. Function equality was reachable from exactly two lines in @flighthq/log -- add_log_sink's includes and remove_log_sink's index_of -- which is why the module could be closed at all. The emit_signal failures were a different defect entirely: 'couldn't deduce template parameter T' through the flight::Ref alias, now answered by the respell-reference-alias repairs, not by anything in this override.

overrides.reason: get_camera3_dfrustum_corners writes `out.element(i_2).x = ...` where `out` is Array<Vector3Like> and Vector3Like is flight::Ref<Vector3>, a std::shared_ptr. The TypeScript is `out[i].x = results[i][0]`, a member assignment THROUGH a reference, and the emitter wrote it as a direct member access on the element: "'std::shared_ptr<flight::types::Vector3>' has no member named 'x'".
overrides.change: Three characters, three times: `.` becomes `->` on the three component assignments. Nothing else in the function changes.
overrides.equivalence: Array::element returns a reference to the stored shared_ptr, so `->x = v` assigns through to the pointee -- the same object the caller passed in, mutated in place, which is what the TypeScript does to the array it was given. No declaration is added or removed, no control flow changes, and the function's result is unchanged.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A source patch cannot reach it: the TypeScript is already correct and idiomatic, and there is no equivalent spelling of `out[i].x = v` that would make the emitter choose `->`. A repair cannot reach it either, for a reason worth stating because the fix LOOKS mechanical: deciding between `.` and `->` requires knowing that the element type is a pointer, which is type information no text rewrite has. There are eleven `.element(...).member` sites in the tree and @flighthq/adjustments compiles with its own, because there the element is a value -- so a textual rule would break the compiling package to fix this one. AGENTS.md names rewriting an operator the emitter emitted as source text as override territory, and this is exactly that.
overrides.unblocks: @flighthq/camera's last three failing headers -- frustum_corners.hpp and the two barrels that include it -- taking camera from 18/21 to 21/21, a complete package. It is 21/21 emitted and had no other defect.
overrides.expires: when the emitter selects the member-access operator from the lowered element type rather than writing `.` unconditionally.

overrides.reason: createEasingSamples is the ONE declaration the emitter refused in @flighthq/easing, and the refusal is about the signature rather than the body: `out?: Float32Array` returning `Float32Array` gives two union domains -- the supplied array and a freshly allocated one -- that land on a single carrier, flight::Float32Array, with no discriminator. Refusing that in general is correct, because the compiler cannot know the two are meant to be the same object.
overrides.change: Writes the function, transcribed from the TypeScript the refusal comment quotes verbatim. 22 of the package's 23 modules were already emitted and all 23 headers already compiled; this is the whole remainder.
overrides.equivalence: The TypeScript states the invariant the compiler could not verify -- "Returns the output array (always the same object as `out` when one is supplied)" -- and flight::Float32Array is a handle onto shared storage, so returning the supplied array returns that same object rather than a copy. The three behaviours the source comments single out are preserved exactly: count=1 samples the MIDPOINT ease(0.5) rather than ease(0); the endpoints are reassigned after the loop to clamp away floating-point drift in i * step, so result[0] is exactly ease(0) and result[n-1] exactly ease(1); and t is read into a local before the write, which the source marks as alias safety because `out` may be a view over memory the easing function also reads. Number.isFinite lowers to std::isfinite, the spelling the emitter uses everywhere else in the tree.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair may only add text with no behavior, and this is a function body. A source patch could in principle rewrite the TypeScript signature to avoid the union, but that would change the public API of a shipped Flight package to suit this profile's compiler, which is a worse trade than writing twenty lines here. The refusal is a genuine limitation of the union lowering, not a defect in the emitted text.
overrides.unblocks: @flighthq/easing: 23/23 modules and 23/23 headers, a 23-module package that was held entirely by one function.
overrides.expires: when the compiler can represent a union whose domains share a carrier but are provably the same object, or accepts the invariant as a declared contract.

overrides.reason: The one refused module in @flighthq/particles contains five missing functions. Its Partial<ParticleEmitterConfig> parameter, string-and-keyof intersections, and closed-key reads have no statically represented C++ object shape, even though every function body operates on the concrete ParticleEmitterConfig carrier and otherwise uses supported control flow.
overrides.change: Supplies all five refused functions as a faithful transcription. A private key dispatcher maps the module's 45 numeric field names to the concrete ParticleEmitterConfig members; normalization replaces non-finite values from a separately created defaults object, copies the normalized object across the TypeScript object-spread identity boundary, then applies the source's curve filtering, flooring, and clamping in source order. Validation appends the same finite, non-negative, lifetime, capacity, frame-count, inverted-range, unit-range, and curve issues in the same order with the same fields, severities, and message text.
overrides.equivalence: The public functions use the exact generated carriers: the same optional partial-input shape accepted by create_particle_emitter_config, flight::Ref<ParticleEmitterConfig>, and Array<Ref<ParticleConfigIssue>>. The returned normalized config is a new reference, matching `{ ...out, overrides }`, while retained curve arrays preserve their reference identity. std::isfinite, std::floor, std::max, std::fmod, flight::to_string, optional absence, and shared Array storage reproduce the corresponding TypeScript operations without changing equality, ordering, null handling, or mutation visibility.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair may only insert declarations with no behavior, while this module needs five bodies. A source patch would have to replace public Partial<T> and Readonly<T> signatures or re-express ordinary keyed validation code solely to satisfy the current C++ shape model; that would distort target-neutral TypeScript instead of addressing the signature-level lowering gap.
overrides.unblocks: @flighthq/particles: its only refused module is supplied, taking the package from 12/13 emitted modules plus 13/13 compiling headers to an assisted, shippable 13/13 package.
overrides.expires: when the compiler can resolve Partial<ParticleEmitterConfig>, string-and-keyof intersections, and closed-key reads against the concrete ParticleEmitterConfig carrier and emit this module faithfully.

overrides.reason: The emitter refused the whole module when AbortSignal.addEventListener reached AbortSignalEventMap through an indexed-access type. That signature-level restriction withheld forty-four declarations even though forty bodies use runtime carriers the SDK already provides.
overrides.change: Supplies the forty representable declarations. Optional host operations retain their documented resolved defaults, already-aborted direct operations return rejected Tasks carrying the signal's reason, and signal presence is forwarded exactly: absence remains std::nullopt while a present signal is passed through. Path normalization, glob matching, recursive discovery, stream chunk writing, and the no-provider symlink, permissions, real-path, well-known-path, and watch defaults follow the TypeScript source.
overrides.equivalence: The override uses the exact generated Readonly structural rows and HostFileSystemCapability callback signatures. Direct wrappers return the host Task unchanged, so host settlement and Task identity are preserved; they reject before consulting an operation when the source does, and distinguish an omitted signal from a present one. Source defaults resolve rather than throw. write_binary_file_chunks retains abort-listener identity through flight::Function, copies each Uint8Array chunk with slice, suppresses writer-abort failures, removes the listener, converts non-abort stream failures to false, and keeps abort as rejection.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair cannot add behavior. Rewriting ordinary AbortSignal.addEventListener TypeScript solely to avoid the emitter's indexed-access computation would distort target-neutral source and would still leave the separately refused dialog runtime projection unresolved.
overrides.unblocks: Forty of the forty-four declarations in @flighthq/filesystem's single refused implementation module; the package remains explicitly incomplete until the dialog runtime projection exists.
overrides.remaining: read_dialog_handle_binary_file, read_dialog_handle_text_file, write_dialog_handle_binary_file, and write_dialog_handle_text_file are intentionally not supplied. Path-backed handles could delegate, but pathless handles require getFileDialogHandleOperations; that function is absent from the refused flight/dialog/file_dialog.hpp, and the generated FileDialogHandle EntityRuntime carrier has no checked projection to FileDialogHandleRuntime::operations. Inventing null/false defaults would change behavior for present operations.
overrides.expires: when the emitter lowers AbortSignalEventMap indexed access and dialog handle runtimes have a generated checked projection to FileDialogHandleOperations.

overrides.reason: The emitter generated detectFontFormat but refused inferFontFormatFromUrl because the optional result of Array.pop reached a member projection without a recorded proof that storage was present.
overrides.change: Adds the one refused function, explicitly testing the pop result before lowercasing and mapping the six supported font extensions.
overrides.equivalence: The query is removed before extension inference, only the final dot-separated component is considered, matching is case-insensitive, woff/woff2 pass through, ttf/otf/eot map to the source's CSS format names, svg passes through, and an absent or unknown component returns nullopt. Array::element(0) is valid because String.split always returns at least one component, while the explicit pop presence check is the proof the source optional chain supplies.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair cannot add a function body. The TypeScript already expresses the presence-safe read idiomatically with optional chaining, so rewriting it to accommodate a lost C++ narrowing proof would make the target-neutral source less clear.
overrides.unblocks: The only refused declaration in packages/font/src/fontFormat.ts. On the current base, generated-only compilation passes 5/9 package headers; supplying this function closes the four dependent failures as well, taking @flighthq/font to an assisted, shippable 9/9 source modules and 9/9 headers.
overrides.expires: when optional chaining after Array.pop records a present payload for the member projection.

overrides.reason: The emitter produced the module constants and public wrappers but refused parseAtfInternal after treating a present nested array element as optional storage at perSlotLevels[slot].push.
overrides.change: Supplies the one refused parser function and the defining type includes the partial placeholder omitted. The transcription validates legacy and versioned headers, declared payload and every length prefix/range; walks side, mip, and format slot order; groups non-empty blocks by GPU-format slot; and returns one TextureContainer per populated slot.
overrides.equivalence: The C++ uses the source's exact format-code sets, three-versus-four slot boundary at version 3, u24 legacy and u32 versioned big-endian lengths, cube face count, log2 dimension guard, signed mip shifts clamped to one, face-major level order, all-zero slot elision, and populated mip count levels.size()/faces rather than the declared header count. Every failure writes the same reason only when a failure object is present and returns nullopt. Array::element(slot) is the source indexed element with proven presence because per_slot_levels is initialized to slot_count arrays before the walk.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair cannot add the parser body. The TypeScript already initializes one inner array per slot before indexed push, so rewriting ordinary, checked array code to accommodate the emitter's lost presence proof would make the source less direct.
overrides.unblocks: The only refused declaration in packages/texture-formats/src/parseAtf.ts. Generated-only compilation passes 7/11 package headers; the override closes parse_atf.hpp and its three consumers, taking @flighthq/texture-formats to an assisted, shippable 11/11 source modules and 11/11 headers.
overrides.expires: when indexed access to an initialized nested Array carries a present payload through member projection.

overrides.reason: The emitter generated the numeric decoder and helper shapes but refused runCffCharstring because readonly arrays of structural {start,end} views could not be stored as owning arrays without changing the nominal CffIndexEntry array identity.
overrides.change: Supplies the one refused Type 2 charstring interpreter. Its public boundary retains the exact Array<Ref<CffIndexEntry>> carrier generated callers already own, while the individual charstring keeps the generated readonly structural row; the body implements operand decoding, width consumption, stems and inline masks, moves, lines, cubic operators, biased local and global subroutines, recursion depth, escaped-operator handling, contour closure, and path replacement.
overrides.equivalence: The interpreter preserves the source's shared input and output identities, clears commands and data before execution, always writes nonZero winding, negates y only at the Path seam, closes an open contour before another move and after unterminated input, applies a leading width only once, counts explicit and implicit stems before skipping mask bytes, shares the operand stack across subroutine calls, uses the three specified bias ranges, and rejects the same truncated operands, masks, absent subroutines, depth overflow, and unknown operators. Direct probes cover all path operator families, 16-bit and 16.16 operands, width and mask rules, local and global calls, depth rejection, empty glyphs, replacement, and implicit closure.
overrides.whyNotAPatchOrRepair: A repair cannot add the interpreter body. The TypeScript signature is ordinary target-neutral readonly structural input, and its callers already pass nominal CffIndexEntry arrays; changing the public source types solely to expose the current C++ carrier would trade away the intended structural API for an emitter storage limitation.
overrides.unblocks: The only refused declaration in packages/font-formats/src/cffCharstring.ts. The package remains at 13/17 independently compiling headers on the current base because all four failures stop earlier in woff_font.hpp at the unrelated missing data_tag_aef43e71dd1e9a6d shape; the override removes the withheld run_cff_charstring declaration behind that blocker but does not claim those headers as newly passing.
overrides.expires: when the compiler can preserve the owning nominal sequence identity while accepting a readonly structural projection of its elements.
